tables.name: companies
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE companies (
            cik TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            entity_type TEXT,
            sic TEXT,
            sic_description TEXT,
            owner_org TEXT,
            insider_transaction_for_owner_exists INTEGER,
            insider_transaction_for_issuer_exists INTEGER,
            name TEXT NOT NULL,
            ein TEXT,
            lei TEXT,
            description TEXT,
            website TEXT,
            investor_website TEXT,
            category TEXT,
            fiscal_year_end TEXT,
            state_of_incorporation TEXT,
            state_of_incorporation_description TEXT,
            phone TEXT,
            flags TEXT,
            former_names TEXT,
            created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        )

tables.name: filings
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE filings (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            cik TEXT NOT NULL,
            accession_number TEXT NOT NULL,
            filing_date DATE,
            report_date DATE,
            acceptance_date_time TEXT,
            act TEXT,
            form TEXT,
            file_number TEXT,
            film_number TEXT,
            items TEXT,
            core_type TEXT,
            size INTEGER,
            is_xbrl INTEGER,
            is_inline_xbrl INTEGER,
            primary_document TEXT,
            primary_doc_description TEXT,
            created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
            UNIQUE (cik, accession_number),
            FOREIGN KEY (cik) REFERENCES companies(cik)
        )

tables.name: financial_facts
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE financial_facts (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                cik TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_value REAL,
                unit TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_category TEXT NOT NULL,
                fiscal_year INTEGER,
                fiscal_period TEXT,
                end_date DATE,
                accession_number TEXT,
                form_type TEXT,
                filed_date DATE,
                frame TEXT,
                dimension_segment TEXT,
                dimension_geography TEXT,
                created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                FOREIGN KEY (cik) REFERENCES companies(cik)
            )

We generally recognize revenues from customers ratably over the terms of their subscriptions. As a result, a significant portion of the revenues we report in each period are derived from the recognition of deferred revenues relating to subscriptions entered into during previous periods. **ServiceNow, Inc. (CIK 1373715) — AI/Now Assist positioning and recent trend**

**Positioning (FY2024 Form 10-K, year ended Dec 31, 2024)**

ServiceNow describes itself as "an early leader in applying AI to enterprise workflows" and positions the Now Platform as "the AI platform for business transformation." Its AI offering, **Now Assist**, is embedded in the platform and sold for certain products **at an additional cost** — i.e., it is a monetized upsell rather than a free feature. Now Assist spans the portfolio (e.g., Now Assist for CSM, FSM, Security Operations, SPM, HR, Legal Service Delivery, Source-to-Pay, Creator, plus industry solutions), and the company says it has "continued to expand the Now Assist product portfolio and plan[s] to continue to embed AI capabilities in our portfolio in the future." (chunks 9600, 11200, 20800, 24000, 25600, 30400, 35200)

The narrative emphasizes **agentic AI as "the next evolution of GenAI"**: AI agents that act autonomously with human oversight and guardrails, available as a Now Assist feature where customers create tailored agentic skills. Differentiation claims include customer choice of ServiceNow LLMs, third-party or own LLMs; built-in AI governance (monitoring, guardrails, benchmarking, adoption/usage analytics); and a single data model/integrated data layer. Ecosystem momentum is cited via NVIDIA (co-developing native AI agents using NVIDIA Agent Blueprints/NIM), Microsoft 365 Copilot integration, and cloud-provider/SI partnerships. (chunks 9600, 14400, 40000, 41600)

**Recent trend — quantitative indicators**

- **Customers with ACV > $1 million:** 2,109 at Dec 31, 2024 vs 1,885 (2023) and 1,626 (2022) — up ~11.9% YoY in 2024 and ~15.9% in 2023 (calculated from disclosed counts; chunk 155200). Growth in large-deal customers decelerated in 2024.
- **RPO:** $22.3 billion at Dec 31, 2024, of which 46% was cRPO; RPO and cRPO rose **23% and 19%** respectively versus Dec 31, 2023 (chunk 153600).
- **Revenue:** total revenues $10,984M in 2024 vs $8,971M in 2023 (+22%); subscription $10,646M vs $8,680M (+23%). Management attributes the increase "primarily [to] increased purchases by new and existing customers" — it does **not** quantify Now Assist's revenue contribution (chunk 182400).
- **Customer base:** ~8,400 customers at Dec 31, 2024 (chunk 41600).

**Interpretation and limitations**

The filing gives no separate Now Assist ACV, attach rate, or AI-specific revenue figure, so the AI contribution to results cannot be isolated from the bundled data; the trend evidence above is company-wide and only directionally indicative of AI-driven demand. The positioning language ("early leader," "uniquely positioned") is management's own characterization, not an independently verified market-share claim. Forward-looking statements about embedding AI further are intentions, not realized results.
